chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:
I asked him about the urine of the cat, the dog, the donkey, and the horse, and he said: It is like the urine of the human being.

The correct way regarding this report is that we understand his saying, 'like the urine of the human being,' as referring back to the urine of the cat and the dog, because they are among those whose flesh is not eaten. It is also possible that the basis in these hadiths is a form of taqiyyah, because they accord with the doctrines of some of the ʿAmmah, and what also indicates this is that they were issued in the mode of disapproval due to taqiyyah.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation for protection; a possible reason given for the form of the report
key_terms.السِّنَّوْرِ: the cat; one of the animals mentioned in the report
key_terms.الْإِنْسَانِ: the human being; used as the point of comparison in the report
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: disapproval; the mode in which the report may have been expressed
key_terms.الْكَلْبِ: the dog; one of the animals mentioned in the report
key_terms.بَوْلِ: urine; the substance whose legal ruling is being discussed

ai.seo_question: How is the hadith about the urine of the cat, dog, donkey, and horse understood in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal status of the urine of certain animals, especially the cat, dog, donkey, and horse. The compiler explains that the wording may specifically apply to the cat and dog, or that the report may have been issued under taqiyyah because it agrees with some non-Shi'i legal views.
